name: Claude Fable (orchestrator)
strategy: Concentrated, unlevered AI-infrastructure conviction in the compute/memory/foundry/networking core (NVDA, MU, AMD, TSM, ANET) plus a small contrarian BTC spot leg, re-based to the 2026-10-19 fill with fresh stops after a nine-session semiconductor washout, at reduced gross (63%) with 37% cash at 4% while the Fed's hike cycle resumes.
reassessment_note: Research done with WebSearch/WebFetch on 2026-10-17. What happened: the 10-14 to 10-16 selloff was macro and positioning, not a demand break. September CPI (released 10-14) printed 3.7% headline / 2.6% core vs 3.6% / 2.5% expected, gasoline +9.1% m/m, pushing December Fed-hike odds to ~94% (Citi now calls a December hike; October 27-28 meeting odds ~15-32%). The same day a chart of CoreWeave's 2031/2032 bond yields (~15-16%, CDS >1,100bp, ~$50B debt) went viral and the 'AI debt' scare hit the whole capex chain: CRWV -16%, AMD -5.7% on 10-14, SOXX down nine straight sessions (longest streak since 2006), Nasdaq -4.5% on the week, VIX to 22. Brent touched $110 on Iran's escalating Hormuz attacks. 10-year ~5.07-5.10% and 30-year ~5.42%, both retreating from the 10-07 peak (30-year fell 10bp on 10-16). What did NOT happen: fundamentals did not break. TSMC reported on 10-15 a record quarter (revenue ~$46.7B above the top of guidance, net income +69% y/y, Q4 guided $52.3-54.3B = +14% q/q, 2026 capex reiterated $60-64B, 2026-28 capex 'significantly higher') and TSM still fell and stopped out of this book at 412.61 on 10-16 - that is a sell-everything tape, not a verdict on foundry demand. Micron's FQ4 beat ($33.42 EPS on $54.2B vs $31.61/$51.1B est.) with a guide above consensus and trades near ~7x forward at ~$880; its 5-day 16% slide was tied to rates and a CXMT China DRAM report, and a buyback restriction lifts 12-09. ASML said it may not be able to meet 2027 demand. BofA argues the AI trade is resilient on GPU utilization; Nvidia's CEO publicly backed CoreWeave. Why trade rather than hold: my 10-05 stops now sit 0.6% (ANET), 2% (AMD) and 3% (MU) away on names that move 4-8% a day. Holding would almost certainly mean getting stopped out at the low of a record losing streak and then sitting in 56%+ cash through any relief bounce, which is the worst of both worlds. Either I believe the mandate or I do not; I do, so I re-base stops to Monday's fill. Why lower gross: the macro genuinely changed since 10-05 - a hike cycle resuming with Brent at $110 is a stagflationary backdrop that compresses high-multiple semis regardless of earnings - so I cut gross from 78% (68% after the TSM stop) to 63%, trim MU from 24% to 16% (highest beta, China-competition overhang, 24% was too much single-name risk), trim AMD 14% to 10%, and re-add TSM at 8% after its record print at a ~15% discount to two weeks ago. NVDA stays at 16% as the highest-quality, least-drawn-down core leg; ANET trims to 8%. BTC stays at 5% unchanged (stop unchanged) as the small contrarian leg - it is in a downtrend (36% off its high, ETF outflows, ~$1B of longs liquidated on the CPI day) but the mandate sized it small for exactly that, and churning it costs 35bps each way. 37% cash at 4% is dry powder for the 10-27/28 Fed decision and the 10-29 PCE print. Known risks I accept: a December hike is now consensus and the Fed could surprise in October; CoreWeave's debt could become a real credit event; oil could spike further. Stops are set to survive one more bad week but not a regime break.

positions.thesis: Highest-quality, most liquid and least-drawn-down core leg (-10% on the 10-05 leg vs -16/-17% for MU/AMD). The CoreWeave scare is about a neocloud's balance sheet, not hyperscaler capex; TSMC's +14% q/q Q4 guide and ASML's 2027 supply warning both point to sustained accelerator demand. Kept at 16% as the anchor; 15% stop re-based to the 10-19 fill.

Memory is the cheapest leg of the AI-infra core: FQ4 EPS $33.42 on $54.2B revenue beat $31.61/$51.1B, guide above consensus, ~7x forward earnings at ~$880, 25% below the June high, and a buyback restriction lifts on 12-09. Trimmed from 24% to 16% because beta ~3, a five-day -16% slide, and a China CXMT DRAM-density report make 24% too much single-name risk in a hike cycle. 18% stop (wider than the others) to respect its daily range.

Second-source accelerator and EPYC CPU exposure; fell 5.7% on 10-14 purely on the CoreWeave read-through, with no company news (Helion rack designs unveiled 10-12, partner configs due in November). Trimmed from 14% to 10% because it is the most sentiment-driven of the compute names and sits 13% below its 52-week high with the AI-debt narrative still live; 15% stop re-based to the 10-19 fill.

Re-entry of the foundry leg stopped out at 412.61 on 10-16, one day after a record quarter: revenue ~$46.7B above the top of guidance, net income +69% y/y, Q4 guided $52.3-54.3B (+14% q/q), 2026 capex reiterated at $60-64B and 2026-28 capex flagged significantly higher. The stock fell on a sector-wide washout, not on the print. Sized at 8% (below the prior 10%) because the macro is worse than on 10-05; 15% stop re-based to the 10-19 fill.

AI back-end networking leg; I found no Arista-specific October news, so its -14% is sector beta plus the CoreWeave/neocloud read-through. Its 10-05 stop sat 0.6% away, so holding would have meant a near-certain stop-out at the low. Trimmed from 9% to 8% and re-based with a 15% stop to the 10-19 fill.

Small contrarian spot leg kept unchanged at 5% with the same 20% stop. BTC is ~$81.5k, 36% off its October 2025 high, with ETF outflows and ~$1B of leveraged longs liquidated on the CPI day, so the trend is against it; but the mandate sized it as a small hedge against the dollar/fiscal picture, churning it costs 35bps each way, and the 20% stop bounds the damage at ~1% of NAV.
